controls.title: Integrate security into the development lifecycle
controls.statement: Build security requirements, responsibilities, design standards, secure coding and risk decisions into the lifecycle for developed and materially changed software.
controls.risk: Software can reach production with avoidable weaknesses when security is considered only after design and development decisions have already been made.
controls.scope: Software, applications, components, services, interfaces and infrastructure code developed or materially tailored for the organisation.
controls.examine: Review lifecycle standards, security requirements, role assignments, design gates, coding practices, training, risk records and monitored performance measures.
controls.interview: Ask product, engineering and security leaders when security decisions occur, who can accept risk and how teams handle urgent changes.
controls.test: Sample recent releases and trace security requirements and decisions from planning through design, development, testing and approval for deployment.
test_steps: Select recent releases, emergency changes and projects using different delivery models and identify required security activities for their risk and lifecycle stage.
Trace security requirements, design decisions, code review, dependency control, testing, findings and approval through source, build and deployment records.
Compare pipeline enforcement with the documented process and attempt an authorised test change missing a required security gate.
Confirm the release is blocked or formally excepted by an authorised owner and that deployed artefacts trace to the reviewed source and build.
controls.expected: Sampled releases show assigned security responsibilities, documented requirements and completed security activities throughout the lifecycle.

mappings.basis: Requires a secure application-development process covering design, coding, training, third-party code, vulnerability management and testing.
Requires a development lifecycle incorporating security and privacy responsibilities and risk management.
Requires secure development practices to be integrated and monitored throughout the software lifecycle.
Requires all internally developed software to use secure development practices.

controls.title: Model threats throughout development
controls.statement: Model likely threats and trust boundaries early enough to change the design, then update the model as the software and threat environment change.
controls.risk: Design weaknesses can remain hidden until exploitation or expensive rework if teams assess only the finished code and overlook how attackers could abuse the system.
controls.scope: New and materially changed software, architectures, interfaces, data flows, trust boundaries and deployment models.
controls.examine: Review threat models, diagrams, assumptions, abuse cases, risk decisions, acceptance criteria, review dates and links to design or backlog changes.
controls.interview: Ask developers, architects and security reviewers how threats are identified, challenged and kept aligned with the implemented design.
controls.test: Sample changed applications and compare their current architecture and exposed entry points with the threat model and resulting mitigations.
test_steps: Select new and materially changed applications and obtain current architecture, trust boundaries, data flows, identities, entry points and dependencies.
Reperform a focused threat analysis with developers and security staff, including abuse of trust, privilege, data flow and external dependencies.
Compare identified threats with the existing model, security requirements, design mitigations, tests and accepted residual risks.
Verify architecture or threat changes trigger model review before release and that unresolved high-risk threats prevent deployment or receive authorised acceptance.
controls.expected: Threat models reflect the implemented system and current threats, identify material attack paths and lead to tracked design or control decisions.

mappings.basis: Requires threat modelling to identify and address application design flaws before code is created.
Requires developer threat modelling and vulnerability analysis with defined context, methods, rigor and acceptance evidence.
Requires threat modelling to support the software development lifecycle.
Requires the software threat model to be reviewed against the as-built software and changes in the threat environment.

controls.title: Test software and remediate security flaws
controls.statement: Use risk-appropriate code review and automated and manual security testing before release and after significant change, then verify that identified flaws are corrected.
controls.risk: Exploitable defects can enter production and remain unresolved when testing is too narrow, occurs too late or produces findings without accountable remediation.
controls.scope: Internally developed and tailored software, components, interfaces, build pipelines and releases.
controls.examine: Inspect the testing strategy, code-review criteria, static and dynamic analysis, penetration or fuzz testing, results, risk decisions and remediation evidence.
controls.interview: Ask engineering and security owners how testing depth is selected, failures block release and unresolved findings are accepted and tracked.
controls.test: Sample releases and trace required tests, findings, approvals and fixes; independently confirm that selected high-risk findings are no longer reproducible.
test_steps: Select releases and components across application types and compare required static, dynamic, composition and manual testing with executed pipeline and assessor records.
Introduce an approved non-production test weakness or use a known safe test case and verify the appropriate tool detects and prioritises it.
Trace sampled high-risk findings to ownership, fix, review, rebuild and deployment without suppression or exception outside the approved process.
Repeat the original test against the released artefact and confirm the weakness is no longer reproducible and no material regression was introduced.
controls.expected: Sampled releases complete the required security checks, material findings have accountable decisions and corrected flaws are verified before closure.

mappings.basis: Requires planned developer testing, evidence, a verifiable flaw-remediation process and correction of identified flaws.
Requires manual review of defined code using specified processes or techniques.
Requires static and dynamic analysis in the application lifecycle to check secure coding practices.
Requires periodic and trigger-based static, dynamic, fuzz or penetration testing for developed and tailored applications.
Describes a maturity progression from manual pre-deployment testing to integrated and automated application security testing.
